Let me start by asking: Can you tell me exactly how your right leg was positioned when the accident happened, and did you hear a "pop" or feel a snap at the time of impact?

Also, when you try to move your leg, does the pain get worse if you try to straighten it against gravity or if you try to lift your heel off the ground?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the mechanism of injury and your description of pain, is there any numbness, tingling, or weakness in your right leg, and can you bear weight on it right now? Also, when you try to straighten your right leg, does the pain worsen significantly or does it feel like the leg is being pulled upward?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Pelvic X-Ray (AP and Inlet/Outlet views) along with Pelvic CT scan.
DIAGNOSIS READY: Anterior Hip Dislocation.
